tb21_profile.skill: Implement a dominant-eigenpair solver (power/inverse iteration or direct 2x2..10x10 char-poly) that is numerically correct to np.allclose yet beats numpy.linalg.eig wall-clock on tiny matrices, i.e. kill Python/LAPACK call overhead, possibly via C/Cython/ctypes.
tb21_profile.domain: Numerical linear algebra in the Python/NumPy/SciPy/LAPACK stack, plus micro-benchmarking of a Python entrypoint.
tb21_profile.task_form: Optimise-for-a-budget: complete a stub function so it is both correct within tolerance and measurably faster than a given reference implementation.

TMax-15K.reason: Deduce an eigenvalue model (graph Laplacian + mass matrix) and write a Python replacement that matches to tolerance and is 10x faster. Same three constraints.
Implement power iteration with Rayleigh quotient for the dominant eigenvalue, plus -O3/gprof profiling. Exactly the algorithm that beats a general eig call.
Hand-implement power iteration for the dominant eigenvector from scratch in C, with normalization and sign determinism. Core algorithm transfers directly.
Replace an O(M*N) numeric kernel with an O(N log N + M) one; must hit 50x speedup while staying within 1e-5. Same accuracy-vs-speed tradeoff.
Keep a Python entrypoint but move the numeric kernel into compiled C for speed - the exact escape hatch TB2.1 allows for beating numpy.
Replicate a solver's handling of near-zero eigenvalues/singular values in numpy/scipy. Same decomposition machinery and tolerance-matching verification.
Randomized power iteration to estimate largest and smallest eigenvalues, parallelised with OpenMP. Same estimator, same speed-vs-convergence tradeoff.
Fix power iteration that oscillates on near-singular/bipartite matrices and parallelise the hot loop. Teaches when naive power iteration fails to converge.
Power iteration for a leading eigenvalue whose OpenMP reduction order makes results nondeterministic; reproducibility of float eigen results.
Serves EIGEN (power iteration dominant eigenvalue) and QR_R (QR decomposition) on 3x3 matrices; small-matrix eigen and QR are the two candidate algorithms here.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Build and install a custom Python C extension module (fastsum) from a spec - the mechanics of dropping a hot Python function into C.
Measure and compare instantiation time of two Python implementations with profiling; teaches attributing Python-level call overhead.
Side-by-side benchmark of merge sort vs bubble sort over 100 iterations; comparing two algorithm implementations by measured runtime.
Benchmark the same program written in asm, C, dash, bash, Python and Node; teaches that language choice dominates tiny-workload runtime.
Computes a median execution time from repeated runs and compares it to a threshold - the same median-of-many-calls metric TB2.1 is scored on.
Time a Python script and write a benchmark report with a pass/fail verdict against elapsed time. Shares only the timing harness.
Julia high-performance chapter: benchmark timings plus compiler introspection. Performance reasoning, wrong language and no linear algebra.
Median of repeated benchmark timings versus a threshold; only the measurement discipline transfers, nothing numeric.
Write a C++ numeric program and validate its floating-point output against a reference tool; correctness-against-oracle shape only.
NumPy array handling with NaNs into pandas. Same library, but nothing about linear algebra or speed.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Solve linear systems three ways and compare numerical accuracy of the solvers; closest thing here to reasoning about a linear-algebra solver's error.
Probe float64 precision limits empirically; the tolerance intuition behind np.allclose, but no algorithm and no speed.
Build a numeric algorithm from source and score it on a benchmark; same build-then-measure loop, different subject matter.
Fixed-point/floating-point conversions with exact expected values; float representation awareness only.
Zero-copy NumPy array view over a C++ std::vector - the buffer-sharing trick used when handing a C kernel back to Python.
Implement N-Queens from a spec with exact output for n=1..11; implement-an-algorithm-correctly genre, no numerics or perf budget.
Implement bubble sort emitting per-pass state; algorithm-from-spec with exact output, unrelated stack.
Julia session including @time of a 1e8-element comprehension and JIT warm-up; timing methodology, nothing else.
Run Louvain clustering on a numeric matrix; matrix-shaped data but the algorithm is invoked, not implemented or optimised.
Compile a native extension into a loadable .so. Only the build-a-shared-object step overlaps; no numerics.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Implement the missing 2D residuals case in linalg.lstsq to match numpy's semantics exactly; least-squares decomposition in the numpy stack.
Fix wrong matrix dimensions, indexing and the recurrence formula in a DP algorithm; index-level correctness of a matrix loop.
Wrong matrix initialisation and iteration bounds in an edit-distance kernel; same class of off-by-one in an iterative matrix update.
Repair the matmul FLOP-count handler; reasoning about the cost of matrix multiplication, which is what the optimisation here trades on.
Match numpy's eye dtype=None default exactly; forces reading numpy's actual dtype semantics rather than assuming them.
Match numpy's full dtype inference for integer fill values; same numpy-semantics fidelity, relevant when hand-rolling array code.
nanmin/nanmax broken for scalar input; edge-case shapes in a numpy reduction, like the 1x1 matrix edge case here.
to_numpy mishandles tensor dimension permutation; array shape/layout bookkeeping between a tensor library and numpy.
Tensor-to-ndarray conversion bug breaking downstream transforms; numpy interop correctness only.
Reason about dtype itemsize to size array chunks; memory-layout reasoning adjacent to array performance work.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: eig() returns the wrong shape for a 1x1 matrix - an eigensolver's own degenerate-size edge case, exactly what a hand-rolled solver must get right.
Eigenvector test fails on AMD CPUs: eigenvector sign/ordering is not uniquely determined, so the check must be invariance-based, not elementwise.
Add a differentiation rule for tridiagonal_solve; implementing a dense linear-algebra routine's math correctly from the literature.
Add transposed= to pt.linalg.solve to avoid an extra transpose Op; a linear-algebra API change motivated purely by saved work.
eigenstates returns eigenvectors with wrong dimension metadata; handling eigenvector output structure in a numeric library.
QubitUnitary problems debugged via eigh/expm and an allclose unitarity check; same tolerance-based validation of an eigendecomposition.
qml.eigvals must honour wire_order when building the eigenvalue matrix; eigenvalue/diagonalizing-matrix bookkeeping.
matmul on conjugate-transposed sparse arrays fails in the numba backend; matrix-product code paths in an accelerated numeric library.
Extend a numba-accelerated matrix-profile kernel with a constant-subsequence flag; editing a hot numeric kernel without breaking its math.
Pyccel's C wrapper must return dicts; Pyccel exists to compile Python numeric functions to C, the same accelerate-a-Python-entrypoint stack.

final_top10.reason: Eigenvalue computation in Python that must match a reference to tolerance and be 10x faster. Nearly the same task.
Power iteration with Rayleigh quotient for the dominant eigenvalue plus -O3 profiling; the algorithm that beats a generic eig call.
Hand-written power iteration for the dominant eigenvector, with normalization and sign determinism, in dependency-free C.
Rewrite a numeric kernel for a 50x speedup while staying within 1e-5 of the reference; identical accuracy-under-speed-budget contract.
Python entrypoint wrapping a compiled C kernel for speed - the exact escape hatch TB2.1 permits.
numpy/scipy decomposition that must reproduce a reference's handling of near-zero eigenvalues; same solver machinery and tolerance check.
Randomized power iteration for the largest and smallest eigenvalues with a convergence-rate budget; same estimator family.
Diagnose and fix non-converging power iteration on near-singular matrices, and speed up the hot loop; both failure modes here.
An eigensolver's degenerate 1x1 case returns the wrong structure; the same edge case a hand-rolled dominant-eigenpair routine must handle.
Power iteration for a leading eigenvalue whose parallel reduction order makes the result nondeterministic; float reproducibility in eigen code.

notes: TMax-15K dominates legitimately: it is the only corpus with tasks that pair an eigen-solver with a wall-clock speedup requirement, and I found several by searching rather than from the shortlist (task_004857_2c3d045e, task_004244_018a965b, task_000042_6e4922c3, task_004322_dc7e237c, task_003789_221005da were all search finds). Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld are genuinely weak here - neither has a numerical-linear-algebra task with a performance budget; their entries are benchmark-harness chores (RTS) or install/build chores (TW) and their low overall scores reflect that, not a shortage of reading. SWE-Smith has no eigen content at all; its best entries are numpy-semantics fidelity bugs in dask. SWE-Rebench's mpmath eig issue is the single defensible non-TMax pick for the top 10. The lexical shortlist was badly polluted by 'power iteration' appearing in PCA/PageRank chores with no perf axis, and by generic '/app/result.txt' boilerplate in RTS.
